content:
Probability punishes careless counting more than weak formulas. One missed case in the sample space, and a clean method still gives the wrong fraction. This free JEE Probability online test checks both your counting and your logic. It holds 15 MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer shows the favourable and total counts. So count slowly, then divide. A clear list of cases beats a rushed guess.

What JEE asks from Probability

  • Classical probability from equally likely outcomes.
  • Addition rule for a King or a red card.
  • Conditional probability and given events.
  • Mutually exclusive and exhaustive events.
  • Real cases like truth telling and dice sums.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Probability is favourable outcomes over total outcomes.
  • P of A or B is P(A) plus P(B) minus P(A and B).
  • Two dice give 36 equally likely outcomes.
  • A leap year has 53 of one weekday with probability 2 over 7.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Counting ordered pairs and unordered pairs together.
  • Adding overlapping events without subtracting the overlap.
  • Forgetting the given condition in conditional probability.
  • Treating a biased die as fair.

Free JEE Probability online test

The 15 question quiz below comes from our verified DPP bank. Keep a pen and rough sheet at hand. First, write the sample space clearly. Then count the favourable cases and answer. Read every explanation you miss, because one lost case shifts the fraction. So take this JEE Probability online test as counting practice.

quiz.title: JEE Probability Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Which of the following is a random experiment?
options: Calculating the area of a circle
Measuring the fixed length of a table
questions.explanation: A random experiment has several possible outcomes you cannot predict. Tossing a coin fits that.

questions.q: A, B and C are mutually exclusive and exhaustive with P(A) = 2P(B) = 3P(C). Find P(B).
questions.explanation: Let P(C) = x. Then P(A) = 3x and P(B) = 1.5x. Their sum 5.5x = 1, so P(B) = 3/11.

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. Find the probability the sum is 8 given that a doublet occurred.
questions.explanation: Doublets give 6 outcomes. Only (4,4) sums to 8, so the conditional probability is 1/6.

questions.q: What is the probability of exactly 53 Sundays in a non-leap year?
questions.explanation: A non-leap year is 52 weeks plus 1 extra day. That day is a Sunday with probability 1/7.

questions.q: Three coins are tossed. Find the probability of all heads given that at least two heads appeared.
questions.explanation: At least two heads gives HHT, HTH, THH and HHH, so 4 cases. All heads is 1 case, giving 1/4.

questions.q: Four letters go into four addressed envelopes at random. Find the probability all land correctly.
questions.explanation: Four letters arrange in 4! = 24 ways. Only one way is all correct, so the probability is 1/24.

questions.q: A card is drawn from 52 cards. Find the probability it is a King or a red card.
questions.explanation: P = 26/52 + 4/52 − 2/52 = 28/52 = 7/13, after removing the two red kings once.

questions.q: p and q are chosen from {1, 2, 3}. Find the probability that x² + px + q = 0 has real roots.
questions.explanation: Real roots need p² ≥ 4q. Out of 9 pairs, only 3 satisfy this, so the probability is 3/9.

questions.q: A card is drawn from 52 cards. Find the probability it is neither a heart nor a king.
A speaks the truth 75% of the time and B 80%. In what percent of cases do they contradict each other?
A speaks the truth 60% of the time and B 90%. Find the probability they agree on a fact.
Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7.
questions.explanation: Six pairs give a sum of 7 out of 36 outcomes. So the probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.q: Three dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers is 5.
questions.explanation: Sum 5 comes from (1,1,3) and (1,2,2), giving 6 ordered ways. So P = 6/216 = 1/36.

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is greater than 9.
questions.explanation: Sums of 10, 11 and 12 give 6 outcomes out of 36. So the probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.q: A number is chosen from 1 to 100. Find the probability it is divisible by 3 or 5.
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3 are 33 and of 5 are 20, with 6 shared. So 33 + 20 − 6 = 47, giving 47/100.
